Updates `TokenBucket.consume` to handle negative time deltas caused by NTP clock corrections. Previously, a backwards clock step drained tokens and locked out requests. The change clamps negative elapsed time to zero, preventing accidental token loss. This ensures the rate limiter remains robust against system clock skew.

The patch prevents the token bucket from draining when NTP corrections cause the clock to step backwards. It modifies `consume` to clamp negative elapsed time to zero, ensuring token refills ignore backward time jumps. It also refactors the capacity clamping and timestamp update logic.

It fixes a bug where system clocks moving backwards (e.g., via NTP) cause negative time deltas. This previously drained the token bucket, locking out users. The code now clamps elapsed time to zero, preventing incorrect token depletion and ensuring the refill logic remains robust against clock skew.

Tokens refill at a fixed rate. Requests consume tokens; if empty, traffic is blocked. This limits data rate while allowing bursts.
It regulates traffic by replenishing tokens at a fixed rate. Requests spend tokens, permitting bursts up to capacity but enforcing a sustained average limit.
It passes requests using tokens from a bucket that refills at a set rate, allowing bursts but rejecting requests when empty.
